_description: Israel Knesset ballot letters -> left/right/other, used by pycensus.census.countries.israel.elections. Israeli politics is organised by camp relative to Netanyahu plus a religious and an Arab axis, not left-right economics. Mapping used: right = Likud + religious-Zionist + Haredi (religious-right) parties; left = the centre-left Zionist camp (Yesh Atid, National Unity, Labor, Meretz); other = Arab parties (Hadash-Ta'al, Ra'am, Balad: opposition parties outside both Zionist camps, ranging from socialist to Islamist) and Yisrael Beytenu (secular nationalist right in ideology but anti-Netanyahu in 2022) plus unlisted minor lists. Edit 'bloc' to change; unlisted letters default to 'other'.

שס.name: Shas
שס.justification: Mizrahi Haredi party; in Netanyahu's religious-right bloc (economically centrist/left-leaning, so 'right' is a camp label).

ג.name: United Torah Judaism
ג.justification: Ashkenazi Haredi lists; religious-right bloc with Netanyahu (camp label, not economic ideology).

פה.name: Yesh Atid
פה.justification: Lapid's centrist/liberal party; leads the anti-Netanyahu centre-left camp. Centrist ideologically, so treated as left only as camp label.

כן.name: National Unity (Gantz-Sa'ar)
כן.justification: Centrist/centre-right ideology (Gantz, Sa'ar, Eisenkot) but opposition camp in 2022; mapped to centre-left camp.

ום.name: Hadash-Ta'al
ום.justification: Arab-Jewish socialist (Hadash) + Arab nationalist (Ta'al) list; left on economics but an Arab party, outside the Zionist camps.

עם.name: Ra'am (United Arab List)
עם.justification: Islamist Arab party; conservative on social issues, pragmatic on coalitions.

ל.name: Yisrael Beytenu
ל.justification: Secular nationalist right (Liberman) but anti-Netanyahu and anti-Haredi; placed in 'other' so the right bloc is not split by camp.
